baseline_validity_note: UNSTABLE across seven real, blind investigator runs against successive revisions of the clean (unmutated) baseline. Six of seven runs raised a flag on the CLEAN corpus itself - most commonly the SPEC-22-41-04/SPEC-22-41-06 pair, even before the mutation was ever applied - despite progressively more explicit reconciling language: an initial floor-combining issue on SPEC-22-41-07 (fixed by redesigning it as an explicit scope-exemption clause, which then held clean); an initial missing occupied/non-occupied-hours carve-out on SPEC-22-41-04 (added); a wording ambiguity in 'normal, continuous operation' being misread as re-invoking the 1.0-3.0 ppm target (removed); full decoupling of SPEC-22-41-06 from SPEC-22-41-04's own numbers and timing (attempted, and it introduced a NEW, previously-never-seen false positive on the previously-always-clean SPEC-22-41-02/SPEC-22-41-05 pair - a possible batch-level 'compounding suspicion' effect worth its own investigation); and finally, restoring explicit non-occupied-hours scoping for shock chlorination (restored) - which STILL did not produce a stable clean reading. Only the very first attempt (before shock-chlorination operational language was added to SPEC-22-41-06 at all) reliably read as clean.
mutation_validity_note: ROBUST and CONFIRMED across all seven real runs: the revised mutation (an explicit chlorine-exposure prohibition plus an explicit isolate/bypass mandate for the dosing system during shock chlorination) was caught 7/7 times with correct anchors (SPEC-22-41-04, SPEC-22-41-06), and the real adversarial-challenge call concluded genuine_defect, explicitly foreclosing all four escape routes based on the mutation's own explicit text ('under any operating condition', naming SPEC-22-41-06's shock event by section reference). The CLAUDE-P21 floor-vs-ceiling finding is confirmed FIXED by this rewording - the remaining problem is entirely at the baseline-validity layer, not the mutation layer.
evaluator_quality_note: The SPEC-22-41-07 false-positive control (redesigned as an explicit non-wetted scope exemption after the floor-combining wording proved unreliable) held clean in every run where the SPEC-04/SPEC-06 pair was NOT independently flagged, suggesting the SCOPE-EXEMPTION pattern is a reliable false-positive-control design, in contrast to the FLOOR-COMBINING pattern (two different minimum thresholds for overlapping equipment), which proved unreliable across multiple wordings and is flagged here as its own separate, real finding worth a dedicated future investigation rather than papering over with more rewording.
added_false_positive_bait: SPEC-22-41-07: a control-panel enclosure explicitly stated to be non-wetted and explicitly exempt from SPEC-22-41-06's scope, despite using minimum-capability (floor) language and chlorine-adjacent context (IP rating in a chlorine off-gas area).
adversarial_review_note: Real, separate model call (final wording): scope, equipment-boundary, operating-condition, and terminology escapes all considered and explicitly foreclosed by the mutation's own text. final_verdict: genuine_defect. final_reasoning: 'All four escape routes are foreclosed by the explicit text of the requirements. Requirement A deliberately extends its 3.0 ppm ceiling to "any operating condition" and explicitly names shock chlorination under SPEC-22-41-06 as the trigger for mandatory isolation. Requirement B's second sentence is an unambiguous operational mandate - not a material procurement standard - requiring the dosing system to remain in continuous operation at 5.0 ppm during every shock chlorination event. Both requirements address the same physical equipment, the same recurring operational event, and impose directly contradictory obligations: one mandates isolation, the other prohibits it. There is no reading of scope, equipment boundary, operating condition, or terminology that resolves this conflict. It is a genuine, material, operationally irreconcilable defect that will arise during every mandated shock chlorination treatment.'
independence_note: Same as the original candidate's review: no alternate model/provider is configured (.env carries only ANTHROPIC_API_KEY). The adversarial challenge and the seven blind investigator runs all used the SAME model family - recorded as a LIMITED, not solved, form of independence. The deterministic ceiling check remains the one genuinely model-independent signal, and it confirms the numeric premise but - as this entire exercise demonstrated - numeric confirmation alone does not settle whether a CLEAN baseline built around that premise will reliably read as clean.
verdict_reasoning: The MUTATION is validated and robust (deterministic check confirmed, adversarial challenge concluded genuine_defect with all four escapes foreclosed, and 7/7 real blind runs caught it correctly with correct anchors) - the CLAUDE-P21 floor-vs-ceiling finding is confirmed fixed by this revision's unambiguous exposure-prohibition/isolation-mandate language. However, the CLEAN, UNMUTATED baseline required to make that mutation meaningful (SPEC-22-41-06's shock-chlorination operational-condition justification) has NOT reliably read as clean across seven real attempts at reconciling it with SPEC-22-41-04, despite explicit occupied/non-occupied-hours scoping stated in both directions. Per CLAUDE-P22's own instruction not to admit merely because clearer wording makes it easier, and given that continuing to reword indefinitely until the model happens not to flag it would compromise the integrity of this validation process itself, this candidate is RETURNED FOR REVISION rather than admitted. The underlying idea - a genuine cross-specification material-performance-envelope conflict, now proven detectable with unambiguous mutation wording - remains sound; the specific clean-baseline construction needed to responsibly license the shock-chlorination operating-condition escape closure needs a different design, not further wordsmithing of this one. This also surfaces two independently valuable findings worth their own follow-up: (1) a reproducible model bias toward reading two different numeric thresholds for related equipment as contradictory even under explicit temporal/scope reconciliation language; (2) a possible batch-level 'compounding suspicion' effect, where a hard-to-resolve pair in a consistency-check batch appeared to correlate with a new false positive on a previously-always-clean, unrelated pair in the same batch.
